analysis:
Examined both changed files.

1) ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift head lines 204-207: enterAddonHold now also cancels selectedModelRecovery.attempt?.task, alongside the existing preloadTasks cancellation. This tightens the TB-012/T-059 model-load fence: a selected-model recovery attempt could otherwise load a model beside the add-on VMs. The addonHoldLoadRefusal fence (head 342-345) remains the authoritative gate. Cancellation only reduces load activity, so no new attack surface is visible. The rest of the file is unchanged: IPC signer identity check (67), owned-hold scoping (115-119), lease and machine-lock enforcement, and persistence.

2) ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift head line 213: after a successful victim unload under an autopilot command, the code now calls noteSelectedModelUnloaded(victim, by: command). The call is presumably bookkeeping that lets selected-model recovery know the coordinator-commanded eviction was intentional, so recovery does not reload the victim. The command is coordinator-authored. TB-002 trusts the coordinator, and existing autopilotRejection and ownership checks still gate it, so no consumer- or provider-controlled input reaches this path.

The implementations of noteSelectedModelUnloaded and selectedModelRecovery were not supplied. Questions for integration:
- Is recovery task cancellation cooperative? Could a recovery that is already past its slot-install check still install? The addonHoldLoadRefusal fence should cover this.
- Does noteSelectedModelUnloaded only suppress recovery, without altering advertised models or attestation and authorization state?

These changes are availability-only (A-018). No effect on encryption, attestation, authorization or billing was identified.
